items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What do you think about Bach and all this new junk they play nowadays? [INTERVIEWEE] This new stuff is alright, this new stuff is alright.

ctx.x: Really? Mr. Tavern? Yeah, it was a tavern. Oh man, that place was like the idea of a band from York. That man made money, I mean he made money, hand over fist. He wanted to keep us, but I don't know, it seemed like them fellas that he had, you know, working there, them guys, they would take the tips. A lot of them guys would steal the tips, you know, and what a little snotty thing, a man handed a dollar and he'd stick it in his pocket, you know. He didn't want us to leave though, he wanted us to, I think his name…
What do you think about Bach and all this new junk they play nowadays?

This new stuff is alright, this new stuff is alright. On the synth, the new stuff they got now, they ain't got no, you might say, no foundation. They ain't got no foundation. Everybody's jumping up and out and in and up, you know, and you can't, you can't tell, you can't get the significance of the piece, you know. That's a hard tune. Yeah, you don't know what they're playing, you can't tell what they're playing. There ain't no lead. And the fellow that's playing the lead should be playing the lead. He's jumping…
